title: P0562 System Voltage Low (diesel)
text: The ECU supply voltage dropped below its minimum while running. Check battery terminals for corrosion and tightness, load-test the battery, then measure alternator output at idle and 2500 rpm (expect 13.8-14.8 V). Inspect the serpentine belt and alternator wiring; replace the alternator or battery if output or cranking voltage is out of range. Clear the code and road-test.

title: P0113 Intake Air Temperature Sensor Circuit High Input
text: The IAT signal reads implausibly high, usually an open circuit or unplugged sensor. Inspect the IAT connector and harness for damage, compare IAT with ambient temperature on a cold engine, and replace the sensor if resistance does not follow the manufacturer's temperature table. Often appears together with MAF faults because many MAF sensors integrate the IAT element.

title: P0102 Mass Air Flow Circuit Low Input
text: The MAF sensor reports less airflow than expected. Inspect the air filter and intake ducting for restrictions or leaks after the sensor, check the MAF connector and supply voltage, and clean the sensing element only with MAF-safe cleaner. If readings stay low at idle versus specification, replace the sensor. Low MAF can cause poor EGR control and reduced power.

title: P0403 EGR Circuit Malfunction
text: The EGR valve actuator circuit has an electrical fault. Check the connector and wiring for the EGR valve, measure actuator resistance against specification, and command the valve with a scan tool to confirm movement. Heavy soot build-up often seizes diesel EGR valves; clean or replace the valve and inspect the EGR cooler for blockage.

title: P0404 EGR Circuit Range/Performance
text: EGR flow or valve position does not match the commanded value. Look for a stuck-open or stuck-closed valve, carbon-blocked EGR passages or cooler, and vacuum/air leaks in the intake. Clean the EGR path and verify position feedback with a scan tool. Persistent faults raise NOx and can trigger limp mode.

title: P2562 Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit
text: The variable-geometry turbo position sensor circuit is faulty. Inspect the actuator connector and wiring, check the reference voltage and signal, and verify the VGT vanes move freely (soot can seize them). Replace the actuator or sensor if the signal is out of range. Expect reduced boost and sluggish acceleration meanwhile.

title: P0234 Turbocharger Overboost Condition
text: Boost pressure exceeded the commanded value, which can damage the engine. Check the wastegate or VGT actuator for sticking, inspect boost-control hoses and the MAP sensor reading, and look for a stuck VGT vane. Reduce load until repaired and schedule service promptly; sustained overboost can damage pistons and turbocharger bearings.

title: P2015 Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor Range/Performance (Bank 1)
text: The swirl/runner flap position is implausible. Inspect the flap linkage and actuator for carbon build-up, check the position sensor signal sweep with a scan tool, and clean or replace the intake manifold flaps. Related to P2009, which indicates the control circuit reads low.

title: P2009 Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Low (Bank 1)
text: The runner control circuit voltage is low, suggesting a short to ground or a failed actuator. Check the actuator harness and connector, measure supply and control voltages, and test the actuator motor. Repair the wiring or replace the actuator; clear codes and verify flap operation.

title: P0107 MAP/Barometric Pressure Circuit Low Input
text: The manifold or barometric pressure sensor signal is below the valid range. Check the 5 V reference, signal wire and ground for shorts or opens, inspect the vacuum hose to the sensor, and compare the key-on-engine-off reading to local barometric pressure (about 100 kPa at sea level). Replace the sensor if the signal stays out of range.

title: P0069 MAP vs Barometric Pressure Correlation
text: MAP and BARO readings disagree when the engine is off or at idle. Verify both sensors read about ambient pressure with the engine off, inspect for clogged air filter or intake restriction, and check connector corrosion. Often a side-effect of a failing MAP sensor (see P0107).

title: P0089 Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Performance
text: Rail pressure is not following the commanded value. Check fuel filter condition and fuel supply pressure, inspect the pressure regulator/metering valve and high-pressure pump, and scan for leaks in the return lines. Reduce load and book service quickly: low rail pressure causes hard starting, power loss and can stall the engine.

title: P0406 EGR Sensor A Circuit High
text: The EGR position sensor reads above its valid range. Inspect the EGR valve connector and wiring for a short to supply, test the sensor reference and signal voltage, and clean or replace the EGR valve assembly if the position feedback is stuck high.

title: Engine Overheating / High Coolant Temperature
text: Coolant temperature above 105 °C. Check coolant level and look for leaks, verify the thermostat opens, confirm the radiator fan operates, and check for a restricted radiator or failing water pump. Reduce load (throttle_load) and let the engine cool; continued operation risks head-gasket damage.

title: Low or High System Voltage
text: Control-module voltage outside 12.6-15.0 V while running. Test the battery and alternator output, inspect the belt, grounds and terminals. Low voltage can degrade sensors and injector control; high voltage indicates a regulator fault and risks damaging electronics.

title: High Intake Air Temperature
text: Hot intake air reduces density and power. Inspect the intercooler and charge-air piping for blockage or leaks, check the air-intake routing, and verify the IAT sensor reading against ambient.

title: Multivariate Outlier Reported by the Anomaly Detector
text: The IsolationForest model flagged the current telemetry as unusual relative to this asset's recent history without crossing a single threshold. Review the trending signals in the Telemetry view, compare them to normal behaviour for the current operating mode, and monitor; schedule an inspection if the outlier persists.

title: Battery Overtemperature
text: Battery temperature above the safe limit accelerates degradation and risks thermal runaway. Pause charge/discharge or reduce current (throttle_load), allow the pack to cool, check the thermal-management loop and ambient conditions, and inspect for a failing cell. Resume only when the temperature is back below 35 °C.

title: Battery Capacity Fade (SOH below 80%)
text: State of health below 80% means usable capacity has dropped noticeably. Fade accelerates at high temperature and high depth of discharge. Limit deep discharges and fast charging, keep operating temperature moderate (eco_mode), and schedule a capacity test. Plan replacement as SOH approaches 70%.

title: Battery Approaching End of Life (SOH near 70%)
text: At about 70% of rated capacity (30% fade) the battery meets the end-of-life criterion. Schedule service and plan pack replacement; reduce duty cycle until then. Capacity will keep falling and range will shrink.

title: Cell Voltage Out of Range
text: Cell voltage below 2.0 V (deep discharge) or above 4.25 V (overcharge) is outside safe limits. Stop the charge/discharge session, verify the charger and BMS cut-off settings, and check cell balance. Cells that were driven out of range should be capacity-tested before returning to service.
